kept.excerpt: Qatar is working with partners in the region and around the world, including China, to resume talks between the United States and Iran, a Qatari foreign ministry spokesperson said. Qatar’s prime minister and foreign minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani, was leading a delegation in Beijing.
kept.publisher: Reuters, via The Times of Israel
kept.relevance: This cutoff-day report establishes active efforts to restart diplomacy, without announcing a date, venue, or confirmed senior-level US-Iran round.

kept.excerpt: Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu held a telephone call with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on September 8. Motegi expressed concern about renewed exchanges of attacks between the United States and Iran, called for talks to resume as soon as possible, and requested Iranian flexibility to avoid prolonging the impasse. Both ministers agreed to maintain close communication toward a diplomatic resolution.
kept.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
kept.relevance: This official statement corroborates the diplomatic impasse at the cutoff and shows external pressure for renewed talks; the Japan-Iran telephone call itself does not meet the qualifying-round criteria.

kept.excerpt: In its September 8 update, the Institute for the Study of War and Critical Threats Project reported nothing significant under its US-Iran negotiations section.
kept.publisher: Institute for the Study of War and Critical Threats Project
kept.relevance: This contemporaneous monitoring assessment provides a limited cross-check on the absence of a major reported negotiation development that day, rather than proof that no private diplomacy existed.

kept.excerpt: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said contacts with regional countries to defuse the war were continuing and described meetings with a visiting Qatari delegation as good. He also said negotiations with Oman over a temporary safe transit route through the Strait of Hormuz were making significant progress. Baghaei blamed Washington for breaching the earlier memorandum of understanding and attributed insecurity in the strait to US attacks and the naval blockade.
kept.relevance: The report identifies functioning mediation channels alongside unresolved grievances, while the reported Iran-Oman and Iran-Qatar contacts alone do not establish participation by senior US representatives in a qualifying process.

kept.excerpt: Vice President JD Vance said the United States was not talking to Iran and would not do so unless Iran stopped shooting at commercial shipping. He presented an end to those attacks as the condition for resuming negotiations.
kept.relevance: A public condition stated by the senior US negotiator identifies a concrete obstacle that would need to change for a new formal round to begin.

kept.excerpt: CNN reported that US-Iran talks had stalled and that the White House had said the preceding Thursday that no negotiations were ongoing. Iran and Oman continued discussions on an arrangement to restore maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, with regional mediators including Qatar backing those discussions. Iranian officials linked navigation through the strait to broader discussions with Washington and regional security developments.
kept.relevance: This late-August status report establishes stalled bilateral negotiations while distinguishing regional maritime diplomacy from a confirmed new senior-level US-Iran round.

kept.excerpt: Switzerland welcomed progress during diplomatic talks involving the mediators, Iran and the United States at the Bürgenstock overnight on June 21–22. It welcomed the establishment of a high-level committee and a roadmap targeting a final agreement within 60 days. The roadmap provided for the immediate resumption of technical discussions.
kept.publisher: Swiss Federal Department of Foreign Affairs
kept.relevance: This official baseline confirms the completed round and the anticipated technical follow-up, whose seniority and formal participation would require separate verification under the resolution rules.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: September 8, 2026, inclusive. Selected seven sources with explicit publication dates on or before the cutoff; no prediction-market pages, odds, later developments, or outcome information are included. Publication dates and factual text were checked against web_search source extracts. web_fetch failed because multiple fetch providers were registered; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so full-page verification was unavailable and no further fallback attempts were made after those errors. Some unrestricted search results were dated after the cutoff and were excluded. The evidence distinguishes calls and regional mediation contacts from a confirmed formal in-person process involving authorized senior representatives of both governments. It does not establish an exhaustive absence of private qualifying meetings or resolve the market.
